statement: A path with an empty segment before its end (`//`, also as removing a path parameter leaves it), an encoded separator (`%2F`, in either case) or a backslash (`\`, or `%5C` in either case) is answered 400 before authentication: a pattern reads them as segments of their own or as part of one, so a DENY would not match what a backend that merges slashes, decodes separators or reads a backslash as a separator serves. A trailing `/` is read as written (in the deny direction, as PIP-35 says), and a double-encoded separator (`%252F`, `%255C`) decodes to text.
